note: Three consecutive items of one shard, with what the server reported for both calls of each. Recorded from a real llama-server on a stock ubuntu-latest runner, not constructed: these are the rows the run itself wrote to state/item-health/2026/09/13.csv, copied here so a test never reads the committed ledger (CLAUDE.md section 13, Guardrail #12). What it is for is the prefix cache - three items is the smallest number that can tell an item-major sequence from a call-major one, because the second item is the first that could have had its prefix evicted and the third is the first that proves it was not a fluke.

provenance.rows: the 161st, 162nd and 163rd rows of state/item-health/2026/09/13.csv, in the order the run appended them
provenance.hardware: github stock ubuntu-latest, 4 vCPU, no GPU
provenance.spread: one run, three items; the fourth consecutive item agrees and is recorded below as a fourth reading rather than as an average

caveat: The system turn was 1,755 tokens on this run. It is not 1,755 today - the prompt files have been edited since, and `idhazh.measured.LABEL_SCAFFOLD_TOKENS` records 2,167 for the whole scaffold with 2,055 of it the system turn. So the assertions over this file are the relationships between the numbers, never the numbers themselves: a prefix figure that is identical across items, and a call-2 prefix that covers the label call's whole prompt. A test that pinned 1,755 would go red the next time somebody improved a sentence, which is a fuse rather than a check.
